title: Swiatek Wins First Title of the Season at Canadian Open
summary:
Have you ever had a rough year and then finally something good happens? That's how tennis star Iga Swiatek must feel right now! On Thursday, she won her first title of the season at the Canadian Open in Toronto. She beat world number two Elena Rybakina in straight sets, 6-2 6-3. It was Swiatek's 26th career title, and she did it in just one hour and 15 minutes!

Swiatek has had a tough time lately. She won Wimbledon last year, but this year she didn't do as well in the big tournaments. She lost to Rybakina in the Australian Open quarter-finals, and she only made it to the fourth round of the French Open and the third round of Wimbledon. People were saying mean things about her on the internet, and it was hard to deal with. But she kept working hard and even hired a new coach, Francisco Roig, who used to work with Rafael Nadal.

After the match, Swiatek said, "It means so, so much to me because the past months were not easy." She also talked about how hard it is to ignore all the opinions people have about you online. But she said she's happy she kept focusing on growing and improving her game.

In the second set, Rybakina led 2-1, but then Swiatek won five of the last six games to finish the match. Rybakina said, "I tried my best but it wasn't enough." Swiatek will now move back into the top five in the world rankings. And there was even a cute moment at the trophy ceremony—a dog came on court! Swiatek's next big test will be the US Open later this month. Maybe she'll win another Grand Slam!
why_it_matters: Swiatek's comeback shows that even champion athletes have bad stretches, and steady work can help them regain confidence.
